credits.title: tweakyourpc
lines: Everyone who builds in the open

scenes.title: Christopher Davis
scenes.tagline: Understands the problem. Directs the machines. Ships the tool.
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc
lines: He works in IT, and he isn't a programmer by trade. He builds software by understanding a problem deeply, then directing AI coding agents until the solution works.
He sets the goals and the limits, tests every result, and keeps it all running on his own hardware.

scenes.title: Six projects
scenes.tagline: Built to run on your own terms.
lines: Here are six of his projects.
Games, knowledge, cities, words, time, and ports.
Each one built to run on your own terms.

scenes.title: Game Night
scenes.tagline: A Google Sheet becomes your game room
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/game-night
lines: Game Night turns a Google Sheet into your own personal game server, for free.
Its star is Wordwright, a crossword tile game in the spirit of Scrabble. Every word is checked against a real dictionary, and there's a computer opponent when friends are offline.
Four in a Row, Checkers, and more play across devices, and every table and replay stays in your own Google Drive.

scenes.title: TextStrata
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/textstrata
lines: TextStrata is a local-first knowledge workspace, with plain Markdown as its storage format.
Every note is classified, tagged, and cross-linked deterministically, with no AI, and every link names the signal that made it.
Originals are never rewritten, and search runs on a local SQLite index.

scenes.title: Vertex City
scenes.tagline: A real city, drawn as light
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/vertex-city
lines: Vertex City draws real places from OpenStreetMap, under an astronomically correct sky.
Click a building to see what the map knows about it, with its Wikipedia summary when there is one, and tune in to radio stations broadcasting nearby.
Speed up time to watch the sun go down and the windows light up, then click a star to learn its name.
With no connection at all, a procedural city is ready to explore.

scenes.title: Wordsmith Studio
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/Wordsmith-Studio-2
lines: Wordsmith Studio finds exact anagrams, then turns them into kinetic typography.
Astronomer becomes moon starer, letter for letter.
Export a GIF or a video right in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

scenes.title: Temporal Lens
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/temporal-lens
lines: Temporal Lens is a browser extension for the threads you read later.
It finds phrases like next Friday or in three days, and shows what they meant when the message was posted.
It is fully local and deterministic: no AI, no accounts, and no network calls.

scenes.title: portbroker
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/portbroker
lines: Portbroker gives every local service a stable, named port before anything binds.
So when an AI coding agent starts its own server, it can't take the port your work depends on.
One dashboard shows what is reserved, what is listening, and where it lives.

scenes.title: Made on this PC
scenes.tagline: Blender and ArtCraft, directed by AI agents
scenes.subtitle: blender.org · getartcraft.com
lines: This film was made the same way: on one small PC, offline, with open-source tools.
Blender built and lit the glowing, floating screens. ArtCraft's EffectCraft animated every title.
And FilmCraft assembled the cut on a real timeline, so any part of it can still be opened and edited by hand.

scenes.title: Why it works
scenes.subtitle: github.com/tweakyourpc/textstrata
lines: AI coding agents in the terminal wrote and ran every step, driving each app through MCP and command-line tools.
The ArtCraft apps are open source, so an agent can script every one of them end to end, and chain them together in ways closed tools like Adobe's don't open up.
TextStrata already holds local knowledge of this whole environment, and the agents can read the source code. So the film came together in a single evening, with minimal direction.
An online video AI service could get close, but only after being fed all of that context. Here, it was already at home.

scenes.title: github.com/tweakyourpc
lines: Find all six projects, and whatever he builds next, at github.com/tweakyourpc.
